messages:
maya: Heads-up — CI flakes when multiple test containers run `redwoodctl login --headless` concurrently. One of the processes just stalls for ~10s and then continues.

jen: I saw this too. Minimal repro in a containerized runner: run two headless logins at once with the same profile and one of them appears to block waiting for the token cache.

simon: Repro confirmed locally on ubuntu docker host. The CLI uses a mkdir-based lock under ~/.redwoodctl/ which races on NFS/overlayfs. One process sleeps waiting for the other to finish writing tokens.

maya: Example output from the hung process:
```
INFO  auth: starting headless login
WARN  auth: waiting for existing token refresh
ERROR auth: token refresh failed: context canceled
```
No browser prompt, just silence until the other process finishes.

luis: Workarounds that helped: serialize logins in CI (single login step), or pre-create a token with `redwoodctl token create --profile $REDWOODCTL_PROFILE` in the entrypoint. Not great but works.

jen: Also noted that in 0.12.x `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE` env var is ignored by `login --headless` unless `--profile` is passed. That tripped our Docker image which relied on the env var.

simon: I opened a draft PR to change locking to use an advisory fcntl-based file lock with exponential backoff and a `--skip-token-cache` flag for ephemeral runners. PR: gh:redwood/cli#458 (draft). The fcntl fallback and atomic rename reduce NFS races.

maya: Nice. Can we also add a `--no-lock` alias? Some CI images lack proper file locking and will still fail with fcntl.

simon: Added `--skip-token-cache` to the branch (opt-out path) and a `--no-lock` alias is doable but I'd prefer `--skip-token-cache` because it documents the behavior (no token persisted). Default keeps cache and locking for normal dev UX.

jen: Tested the branch in a GitHub Actions matrix (ubuntu / macOS / self-hosted runner). Races no longer block on linux containers. WSL still had one edgecase due to stale symlink handling; I left a note in the PR.

luis: One more ask: can we improve how headless login picks up profile from env? Right now it's inconsistent across subcommands. It should honor `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE` unless explicitly overridden.

maya: Agreed — update docs for profile precedence. Also add a small snippet to devex docs with a docker-entrypoint example:
```
#!/bin/sh
set -e
: ${REDWOODCTL_PROFILE:=ci}
# create token (best-effort) so parallel tests don't race
redwoodctl token create --profile "$REDWOODCTL_PROFILE" || true
# run tests
exec "$@"
```
This avoids login races and keeps logs clean.

jen: Filed a GH issue for the retry storm I saw: the CLI was re-posting token refresh requests 3x immediately with no jitter, which messes up our auth metrics. I'll attach logs.

redwoodctl-bot: CI: cli-unit-tests for gh:redwood/cli#458 passed on linux-amd64 :white_check_mark: (artifact: build/logs/1234).

maya: Cool — once the locking PR lands let's do a short announcement in devex and add the snippet to onboarding. Leaving this thread for triage. If anyone sees post-merge hangs, ping @simon with the raw logs and runner details.
